Author and game designer Rizwan Virk joins the Joe Rogan Experience for episode 2151 to talk about simulation theory. Virk wrote a well-known book arguing that our world could be a vast computer simulation. It is the kind of big idea Rogan loves to test for hours.

Virk lays out the case step by step, from fast gains in games and virtual worlds to old religious ideas that rhyme with it. Rogan asks what proof could ever settle the question. The episode is a friendly, far-out tour of a theory that treats physics, faith, and video games as parts of one puzzle.

Bob Lazar and filmmaker Jeremy Corbell join the Joe Rogan Experience for episode 1315, one of the show's most watched episodes. Lazar claims he worked on alien craft at a site near Area 51 in 1989. Corbell, who filmed Lazar's story, sits beside him as a backer and witness.

Lazar retells his account in detail: the bus rides, the hangar, and the reactor he says he saw. Rogan probes the weak spots while Corbell adds context from his film. Believers and doubters both use this episode as the fullest version of a story that shaped modern UFO culture.

Ben van Kerkwyk hangs with Rogan for episode 2374 of the Joe Rogan Experience. Van Kerkwyk makes the UnchartedX videos, field studies of ancient sites and the tool marks left on old stone. On this visit, though, the tone stays loose and easy, more hang than lecture.

The two talk without an agenda, trading stories and laughs across a long, open session. Listeners who know van Kerkwyk's careful site work will hear the relaxed man behind it. The episode is kept as a full record of the visit, a reminder that the show's engine is often just two people enjoying a long talk.
